skill: Applied maths, statistics and scientific practices
expected_level_description: You can: - apply designated quantitative techniques such as time series analysis, optimisation and simulation to create and embed appropriate models for analysis and prediction - provide guidance on matching data sources with relevant applied mathematics and statistical techniques to meet analysis goals - apply appropriate statistical techniques to available data to discover new relations and offer insight into research problems, helping to improve organisational processes and support decision making - access and use the statistical tools available within the organisation

skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations - manage active and reactive communication - support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders

You can: - work with stakeholders to identify and address ethical and privacy concerns - demonstrate and communicate how data ethical issues fit into the wider organisational context - research developments in data ethics and privacy to improve compliance and processes - assess and constructively challenge proposed data ethics policies

You can: - demonstrate practical knowledge of data science tools and techniques - develop data science solutions that maximise insight - identify opportunities for how data science can improve data practices

You can: - collaborate with others when necessary to review specifications - use the agreed specifications to design, code, test and document programs or scripts of medium-to-high complexity, using the right standards and tools
You can: - define the integration build - co-ordinate build activities across systems - understand how to undertake and support integration testing activities

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - read and use FHIR resources, profiles, and APIs - build or test simple integrations under guidance - check messages against a specification
You can: - follow a software life cycle process that meets medical device standards - produce the records that such a process requires

skill: Safe and fair AI in health care
expected_level_description: You can: - plan the validation, bias assessment, and live monitoring of a model with clinical colleagues - decide when a model needs retraining, restricting, or withdrawing - advise teams on when a model may be regulated as a medical device and what evidence it needs
